title: Example 14-3: Stage Directions After a Speaker’s Name

illustrates.quote: Follow print placement and punctuation when stage directions or cues follow the speaker’s name.

blocks.speaker: Anne.
blocks.text: Anne. [laughing] Isn’t that a beautiful balloon?

print.notes: The speaker's name is followed by print's own period, then a stage direction enclosed in square brackets, then the dialogue, all on the same braille line (14.1.6).
print.printFeatures: Single line of dialogue with an inline, bracket-enclosed stage direction; regular typeface throughout.

braille.notes: 1-3 margins for the speech (14.5.1a); print's own square brackets around the stage direction become UEB's own enclosure indicators.

resolution: A/B agreed on braille (byte-for-byte) and on speaker/text substance, but split on structure: A kept speaker/text as separate fields with the name repeated as speaker only, B folded the whole line (including the name) into one text string. Per buildModel14's own design (a 'speech' block's structural driver is the fully pre-composed `text`, exactly as every other section's own builders compose text/segments before textOrSegments), B's shape (name folded into text, with print's own period kept) was kept, since 14.1.6/14.4.1b require the name, its own print punctuation, and the dialogue on one flowing line with no separator this schema would otherwise have to invent. Forward-translated through Emboss's translator ({type:'play', subtype:'prose'}, 1-3 margins): EXACT MATCH (see differences.md).
